officials.name: Chad E. Warbington
officials.bio: Chad Warbington was born and raised in Lawrenceville, Ga. He attended Georgia Tech and received a Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering in 1995. After graduating from college, Chad moved to Albany to start his engineering career at Procter and Gamble.

officials.name: Colette Jenkins
officials.bio: Colette Jenkins, who was born and raised in Albany, Georgia, serves as City Commissioner for Ward 5, bringing a strong foundation in public service, leadership, and community engagement. Her experiences guide her commitment to transparency, fairness, and responsible decision-making for Ward 5 and the City of Albany.

officials.name: Diana Brown
officials.bio: Diana Brown was born and raised in Tifton, Georgia, before making Albany her home for 27 years. Her journey has been a testament to her unwavering passion for advocating on behalf of people, with a career dedicated to empowering the marginalized. As Commissioner for Ward 6, she continues her life's dedication to fighting for human rights and building a brighter future for her community.

officials.name: Jon Howard
officials.bio: Jon Howard was elected to the Ward 1 City Commission seat in 1993 and has been re-elected, with his current term set to expire in 2028. He currently serves on the Pension Board of Trustees and the KADB Board. Commissioner Howard attended Dougherty High School and Albany State University and recently retired from the State of Georgia Crisis Stabilization Unit.

officials.name: Vilnis Gaines
officials.bio: Commissioner, Ward III Began: 1/10/2022 End: 1/2026

officials.name: Willie C. Weaver Sr.
officials.bio: Willie C. Weaver, Sr., was born in Manchester, Georgia, and raised in Albany, Georgia, graduating from Dougherty High School. He served thirteen years in the U.S. Army as a medical specialist before earning a Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science and a Juris Doctorate Degree from Mercer University. After practicing law for over thirty years, he served on the Dougherty County School Board and as Chief Judge of Albany Municipal Court before being sworn in as City Commissioner for Ward 2 in June 2025.

officials.name: Bo Dorough
officials.bio: Bo Dorough is a native of Cordele and a graduate of Georgia Southern College (1983) and the University of Georgia School of Law (1986). He has practiced law in Albany since 1987 and previously served as Commissioner for Ward IV from 2000 to 2007.

officials.name: Conor Sen
officials.bio: Conor Sen was appointed to serve as Brookhaven's District 2 Council Member. He has served on Brookhaven's Planning Commission for 10 years, including two as Chair, and was a member of the City's 2022 Charter Review Commission. Sen is the founder of Peachtree Creek Investments and a former Bloomberg Opinion columnist.

officials.name: John J. Funny
officials.bio: A Brookhaven resident since 2010, District 4 Councilman John J. Funny and Mayor Pro Tempore was elected in November 2021 and sworn into office on January 4, 2022. He was subsequently re-elected in 2026 to serve another four-year term. Councilman Funny is also the President and CEO of Grice Consulting Group, an internationally recognized city/urban planning, traffic engineering, and transportation engineering consulting firm.

officials.name: Madeleine Simmons
officials.bio: Madeleine Simmons was elected in November 2019 to represent District 3 and was re-elected unopposed in November 2023. As Councilwoman, she has championed initiatives such as gaining ownership of Brookhaven Park, building Langford Park, and leading on mental health crisis intervention funding. She is also an equity partner at Stewart Miller Simmons Trial Attorneys and President of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

officials.name: Michael Diaz
officials.bio: Michael Diaz was elected to the City of Brookhaven City Council District 1 in December 2023 and was sworn into office on January 8, 2024, to serve a four-year term. He has been a dedicated member of the Brookhaven community since 2009, serving on the City's Planning Commission and the Peachtree Creek Greenway Board of Directors. Professionally, Michael is a Civil Engineer specializing in Water and Wastewater.

officials.name: John Park
officials.bio: After winning the general runoff election on December 4, 2023, Mayor John Park was sworn into office as Brookhaven's fourth mayor on January 8, 2024, to serve a four-year term. Mayor Park previously served as Brookhaven's District 2 Councilman beginning in November 2014 in a special election. In 2017 and 2021, then-Councilman Park was reelected for his second and third terms.

officials.name: Robbie Cheek
officials.address: 200 E 4th Street P.O. Box 99 Woodbine, GA 31569
officials.bio: A lifelong resident of Camden County, District 1 Commissioner Robbie Cheek can trace his family roots back many generations. With deep ties to the community and a strong desire to help shape its future, Robbie is committed to ensuring Camden County remains a premier place for all citizens, both now and in the years ahead.

officials.name: Chester A. Ellis
officials.bio: A lifelong resident of Chatham County, Chairman Chester A. Ellis is committed to investing in this community and its citizens. He is a proud graduate of Sophronia Tompkins High School and Savannah State University, holding a Master's Degree from Cambridge College. Elected Commissioner for District 8 in 2017, he now serves as Chairman and is the pastor of St. Paul Missionary Baptist Church.

officials.name: Aaron "Adot" Whitely
officials.bio: Aaron “Adot” Whitely is a dedicated father, visionary community advocate, accomplished entrepreneur, and a leader in small business development. He currently serves as the District 6 Commissioner on the Chatham County Board of Commissioners, where he works tirelessly to champion equitable development, expand access to opportunity, and uplift the voices of his constituents.

officials.name: Anthony Wayne Noha
officials.bio: Biographical Information Coming Soon.

officials.name: Dean Kicklighter
officials.bio: Dean Kicklighter is married to Tammy Bower Kicklighter and they are proud parents of four children and five grandchildren. A lifelong resident of West Chatham County, he grew up in Garden City and now resides in Pooler, GA. Commissioner Kicklighter owns and operates two family businesses, Randell & Dean’s and Hardcore 24 and Randell’s 24 Hour Gym, both located in Garden City.

officials.name: Malinda Scott Hodge
officials.bio: Commissioner Hodge was elected to the Chatham County Commission in 2023. She is a lifelong resident of Chatham County and holds a degree in Marketing from Harris University. Malinda is committed to serving her community with humility, focusing on infrastructure, progression, and economic development.

officials.name: Marsha Buford
officials.bio: Reverend Marsha Buford is the Founder and Pastor of The House of Favor Full Gospel Ministries, Inc., where she has served in ministry leadership for the past 19 years. From 2010 to 2023, she also worked as a Job Coach with the Family Restoration Network’s Workforce Development Program. She currently teaches the Fatherhood Program at the Smith Transitional Center in Claxton, Georgia.

officials.name: Tanya Milton
officials.bio: A Savannah, Georgia native, Tanya Milton has a long career in the newspaper business, currently serving as Vice President and Advertising Director of The Savannah Tribune. She is in her 2nd term as 5th District Chatham County Commissioner, actively involved in community leadership and several service organizations. She is married to Walter Thomas and has two daughters and two grandchildren.

officials.name: Skip Henderson
officials.bio: I am Skip Henderson, the 70th Mayor of Columbus Ga. On behalf of our City Council and over 3,000 City Employees, welcome to Columbus, Georgia, a great place to live, do business, work, and play. Columbus Consolidated Government is Georgia's first consolidated government and is proud to serve as a model for other local governments across the nation.

officials.name: Lorenzo L. Heard
officials.bio: Reverend Lorenzo L. Heard is the Chairman of the Dougherty County Board of Commissioners, elected in May 2022. He has a long history as a pastor, currently serving at Greater 2nd Mt. Olive Baptist Church in Albany, Georgia, and is known for his community outreach and leadership.

officials.name: Dr. Romona Jackson Jones
officials.address: 8700 Hospital Drive 3rd Floor, Douglas County Courthouse Douglasville, GA 30134
officials.bio: Dr. Romona Jackson Jones serves as Chairman of the Douglas County Board of Commissioners. She was first elected in 2016, becoming the first African American to hold the position in the county’s 155-year history and the first African American female to be elected Commission Chair in a countywide race in Georgia history. She has been re-elected twice as Douglas County Commission Chairman, both in 2020 and 2024.

officials.name: Annetta Stembridge
officials.address:
Douglas County Courthouse
8700 Hospital Drive
Douglasville, GA 30134
officials.bio: Madam Clerk Annetta Danley Stembridge, elected as the Douglas County Clerk of Superior and State Court in Douglas county in 2020, is the first Black person to hold this title. She was born in Winston, Georgia, and has been a Douglas County resident her entire life. Her goal has always been to serve the citizens of Douglas County.

officials.name: Henry Mitchell III
officials.bio: Commissioner Henry Mitchell III is a native of Atlanta, a U.S. Army veteran, and a broadcasting industry professional known as "Mitch Henry." He is currently the Vice President of REACH Media Network Operations and has served on the Douglas County Board of Commissioners for multiple terms, also sitting on several local boards.

officials.name: Mark Alcarez
officials.address: 8700 Hospital Drive 3rd Floor, Douglas County Courthouse Douglasville, GA 30134
officials.bio: A lifelong resident of Douglas County. Married to my wife Jodi for 27 years with two children.

officials.name: Martin Raxton
officials.address: 8700 Hospital Drive 3rd Floor, Douglas County Courthouse Douglasville, GA 30134
officials.bio: Martin Raxton is a seasoned executive who is delivering programs resulting in increased revenue, improved organizational efficiency and new innovative technology producing measurable results impacting P&L. He has implemented strategic initiatives across large and mid-cap companies resulting in measurable alignment with the mission and goals while operationalizing market concepts producing enterprise level growth. He has directly created strategic governance to track benefits realization outcomes for corporate boards and key executives.

officials.name: Whitney Kenner Jones
officials.address: 8700 Hospital Drive 3rd Floor, Douglas County Courthouse Douglasville, GA 30134
officials.bio: Attorney Whitney Kenner Jones is the owner and managing member of Kenner Jones Law, LLC. She holds degrees from The University of North Carolina at Greensboro, Strayer University, and Mercer University Walter F. George School of Law. As District 2 Commissioner, she is a passionate advocate dedicated to helping and supporting her community through social justice advocacy and legal representation.

officials.name: Renee Godwin
officials.bio: Renee Godwin is a long-time resident of Douglas County with over 27 years of experience as a law enforcement professional in the Metropolitan Atlanta area, including serving as a Douglas County Deputy Sheriff. She is a Georgia Certified Peace Officer and a State Certified Assessor for the Georgia Police Accreditation Coalition. Renee graciously thanks the citizens in Douglas County for entrusting her to serve as their County Coroner.

officials.name: Damon Rahn
officials.bio: Damon Rahn serves as Chairman-at-Large of the Effingham County Board of Commissioners, a position he began in January 2025. He previously served on the Rincon City Council and has a professional background in technology and project management. As chairman, he emphasizes responsible growth, infrastructure planning, and community engagement.

officials.name: Beth Helmly
officials.bio: Beth Helmly serves as the Effingham County Commissioner for District 4, a position she began in January 2025. In this role, she represents District 4 residents on the Board of Commissioners and works to guide county policy, planning, and public services. A retired educator, she previously served on the Effingham County Board of Education from 2014 to 2019.

officials.name: Forrest Floyd
officials.bio: Forrest Floyd serves as the Effingham County Commissioner for District 1, representing residents of the district on the Effingham County Board of Commissioners. In this role, he works with fellow commissioners to guide county policy, oversee public services, and support infrastructure and community development throughout Effingham County. Floyd is a local business owner and has long been active in the community, providing perspective on economic development, responsible growth, and supporting Effingham County’s local business community.

officials.name: Jamie DeLoach
officials.bio: Jamie DeLoach serves as the Effingham County Commissioner for District 3, where he represents residents of the district on the Effingham County Board of Commissioners. First elected in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, he works with fellow commissioners to guide county policy, infrastructure planning, and the delivery of public services. Professionally, DeLoach works in the banking industry and serves as a banker with Ameris Bank.

officials.name: Phil Kieffer
officials.bio: First elected in 2010, Phil Kieffer represents Effingham County’s Fifth District, bringing thirteen years of service and leadership that have fostered economic growth and recreational opportunities. A lifelong native, he holds a B.S. from Georgia Southern University and is president of Phillip Kieffer Construction. He is a member of Springfield Oaks Church and enjoys spending time with his wife, Brandi, and their three sons playing baseball, golfing, hunting, and fishing.

officials.name: Roger Burdette
officials.bio: Georgia native Roger Burdette has proudly served Effingham County as District 2 Commissioner since 2018. A U.S. Navy veteran, Roger earned his BBA from Valdosta State University and later received his MBA from Mercer University, graduating with highest honors while maintaining a 4.0 GPA. Roger is an Effingham County small business owner and has been an entrepreneur since 2001, creating many local jobs and operating several small businesses throughout his career.

officials.name: Abigail Guzman
officials.bio: Abigail Guzman is a local entrepreneur and the Gainesville City Council’s first-ever Hispanic representative. She owns two popular restaurants and a boutique cleaning company in Gainesville. As a voice for Ward 4, her Mexican-American heritage and business experience bring a fresh perspective to the City’s governing body.

officials.name: Bob Norton
officials.bio: Bob Norton was elected to serve the City of Gainesville as the Ward 1 representative. Norton is completing the unexpired term of former Ward 1 council member, the late C. Danny Dunagan Jr.

officials.name: Jon Elliott
officials.bio: Jon Elliott was elected to serve the City of Gainesville as the Ward 2 representative in a November 2025 special election. Elliott is completing the unexpired term of former Ward 2 council member Zack Thompson, now mayor, who resigned from his seat in June 2025.

officials.name: Zack Thompson
officials.bio: Zack Thompson serves as mayor of the City of Gainesville. Before securing the title of mayor, Thompson served as Ward 2 representative for nearly a decade, from November 2015-June 2025.

officials.name: David Gibbs
officials.bio: David Gibbs, 55, is a lifelong Hall County resident, retired firefighter, and local business owner. As Commission Chairman, he is committed to improving infrastructure, fostering economic growth, and ensuring fiscal responsibility, while prioritizing community engagement and public safety. He aims to make Hall County a place where families thrive and businesses grow.

officials.name: Billy Powell
officials.bio: First elected in 2004, Commissioner Billy Powell is a Hall County native and a commercial realtor. He holds a degree in Industrial Engineering and uses his project management experience to push for efficient government and better service to citizens. As a member of the Hall County Board of Commissioners, he is active in SPLOST infrastructure projects and strives to be a good steward of taxpayer dollars.

officials.name: Gregg Poole
officials.bio: Commissioner Poole was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2022. He represents District 3, which covers East Hall and North Hall. Commissioner Poole is a lifelong Hall County resident. He and his wife have one child and they reside in East Hall.

officials.name: Kathy Cooper
officials.bio: South Hall farmer and businesswoman Kathy Cooper was elected to her first term on the Hall County Board of Commissioners in 2014. As District 1 Commissioner, she focuses on addressing the needs of her constituents, maintaining smart growth strategies, and family values. She and her husband operate a cattle and chicken operation and a Christmas tree farm.

officials.bio: Ty Clack is a Christian, husband, and father with a successful career in sales and a passion for serving his community. A proud seventh-generation Georgian, Ty was born and raised just south of Jackson County in Lawrenceville, GA. He graduated from Central Gwinnett High School, attended the University of Georgia, and began his professional journey with PlyMarts Inc.

officials.name: Donald Lovette

officials.bio: Donald L. Lovette is a native of Liberty County, Georgia, and a 1973 graduate of Bradwell Institute High School. He is retired as the Director of Laboratory Services for Liberty Regional Medical Center, Hinesville, and has served as Chairman of the Liberty County Board of Commissioners since 2012.

officials.name: Connie Thrift
officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313
officials.bio: Commissioner Connie Thrift, a lifelong resident of Liberty County and a 1979 Bradwell Institute graduate, has served on the Liberty County Board of Commissioners for twenty years since her first election in 1999. She co-owns Thrift Auto Repair with her husband John, and is actively involved in the community, including serving as Secretary of Diversity Health Center and Chair of Canoochee Electric Membership Cooperative.

officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313

officials.name: Gary Gilliard
officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313
officials.bio: Commissioner Gary Gilliard was born as Robert Gary Gilliard to the late Sergeant Robert and Jackie White Gilliard. He is currently the oldest of four children; he lost an older sister the week of his graduation. He was born on Fort Stewart and grew up in the Rebecca Street Public Housing Development.

officials.name: Justin L. Frasier
officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313
officials.bio: Commissioner Justin Frasier was born in Liberty County to the late Charles Frasier and Mrs. Shirley Frasier. He is a 1999 graduate of Liberty County High School and later attended Morris Brown College, graduating in 2003, and is currently pursuing a Masters in Public Administration. He became the Commissioner of District 2 in 2012, is active in the community, and is married with two children.

officials.name: Marion Stevens, Sr
officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313
officials.bio: Commissioner Marion Stevens is the oldest of five children, reared in the Midway community of Liberty County. He is a 1968 graduate of Liberty County High School and served as a paratrooper in the US Army for four years. He has been active in the Midway community for many years, serving as a volunteer firefighter and medical responder, and has been a County Commissioner since 1999.

officials.name: Timothy Blount
officials.address: 112 N Main Street Room 201, Courthouse Annex Hinesville, GA 31313
officials.bio: Mr. C. Timmy Blount is a life-long resident of Liberty County, a 1984 graduate of Bradwell Institute, and is married with three adult children and six grandchildren. He has a background in construction and forestry, and currently serves as a project manager for a government contractor.

officials.bio: Bill Slaughter is a retired business owner of a family owned and operated business in Lowndes County, serving as the CEO of Waller Heating & Air Conditioning. He has been involved with many civic groups, trade associations, and community boards. His business background helps him ensure Lowndes County maintains fiscal responsibilities while preparing for growth and enhancing community partnerships.

officials.name: Demarcus Marshall
officials.address: 327 N. Ashley St. 3rd Floor Valdosta, GA 31601
officials.hours:
Monday through Friday
8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: Commissioner Demarcus Marshall is a native of Lowndes County and a veteran of the United States Marine Corps and Army. He retired from the City of Valdosta in August 2024 and has served in various civic organizations and taught at Georgia Military College and Valdosta State University. He holds a PhD in Public Policy and Administration.

officials.name: Joyce E. Evans
officials.address: 327 N. Ashley St. 3rd Floor Valdosta, GA 31601
officials.hours: Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: Commissioner Joyce Evans was elected to represent Lowndes County, District 1 in 1996 and re-elected in 2000, serving until 2004. After a short absence, she was again elected in 2008 to represent District 1 through 2012. Joyce brings expertise and years of experience in public/human services and business ownership/management to the Board of Commissioners.

officials.name: Mark Wisenbaker

officials.bio: Commissioner Tally M. "Mark" Wisenbaker, Jr. is a native of Lowndes County, born October 10, 1951 in Valdosta, Georgia. He is a 1970 graduate of Woodward Academy and a graduate of Valdosta State College with a BBA in Management. His experiences and opportunities will greatly contribute to his position as a Lowndes County Commissioner, helping him serve the community positively and effectively.

officials.name: Michael Smith
officials.address: 327 N. Ashley St. 3rd Floor Valdosta, GA 31601
officials.hours:
Monday through Friday
8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: Michael Smith is the CEO of the Greater Valdosta United Way and a lifelong resident of Valdosta, holding a Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance from Valdosta State University. He is passionate about serving the citizens of Lowndes County, striving to inspire positive change and growth while being fiscally responsible. Commissioner Smith is married to Leslie Smith, has five children, and is a member of Park Avenue Church.

officials.name: Scott Orenstein
officials.address: 327 N. Ashley St. 3rd Floor Valdosta, GA 31601
officials.hours:
Monday through Friday
8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
officials.bio: Commissioner Scott "Scottie" Orenstein is a lifelong resident of Lowndes County and a graduate of Valdosta High School. He previously worked at Valdosta State Prison and has been a Licensed General Contractor/President of South Georgia Construction & Consulting since 1997. Orenstein is actively involved in the community, serving on various boards and organizations, and is married with two children.

officials.name: Lester Miller
officials.bio: Lester M. Miller is the second Mayor of Macon-Bibb County's Consolidated Government and the community's first mayor in 13 years. An attorney, small business owner, and lifelong resident of Middle Georgia, he is recognized as a community leader. He and his wife, Toby, have been married for 32 years and raised their two sons in Macon-Bibb.

officials.name: Marcello Banes
officials.bio: Chairman Marcello Banes was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2016. He is a life-long resident of Newton County, an ordained minister, and was the Operations Manager of Banes Transport, LLC. He is dedicated to community leadership and his vision of #OneNewton.

officials.name: J.C. Henderson
officials.bio: In 1976 I graduated from Newton County High School and after high school I attended DeKalb Community College. I am married to Sandy Henderson and we have eight children, Mandy, Quint, Jessie, John, Anthony, Jaquan, Nikeshia and Nikeria. We are members of the Rising Son Christian Church where I serve as Chairman of the Deacon Board.

officials.name: LeAnne Long
officials.bio: LeAnne Long brings experience in the business community and government sector to her role as District 5 Commissioner. She has been married to her husband Stanley for 37 years, living in the core of District 5 with her two children.

officials.name: Stan Edwards
officials.bio: A life-long resident of Newton County, Stan Edwards was elected to the Board of Commissioners in 2016. He retired from AT&T in 2018 after 34 years and now manages an insurance agency's Covington office. He previously served on the Newton County Board of Elections and Board of Education.

officials.name: T. Demond Mason
officials.bio: Demond Mason is a native of Tulsa, Oklahoma and has resided in Georgia for 18 years. He received his Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from Oklahoma City University and in 2020 he was honored with an Honorary Doctorate in Humanitarianism for the work he has done as a Newton County Commissioner. He worked for The Coca-Cola Company for 16 years in Project Management and recently transitioned into entrepreneurship.

officials.name: Andre Cooper
officials.bio: Andre Cooper brings over 24 years of law enforcement, investigative, and public service experience to his role as Interim County Commissioner. A former Deputy Sheriff and investigator, he has focused his career on public safety, accountability, and community trust. As Commissioner, he champions infrastructure improvements, transparent government, and fair, responsive service for District 3.

officials.name: Tameka Allen
officials.bio: Tameka Allen is a visionary innovative strategist who has served as Administrator since September 2024, bringing over 30 years of experience in the technology sector and leadership roles, including Chief Information Officer and Deputy County Administrator for the City of Augusta. She holds an MBA from Augusta State University and a BS in Computer Science from Savannah State University, along with various government management certifications. Ms. Allen is actively involved in technology associations and community boards, and is married with two sons.

officials.name: Garnett L. Johnson
officials.bio: Garnett Johnson is the 85th Mayor of the City of Augusta and the Owner of Augusta Office Solutions and Modern Business Workplace Solutions. With locations in Augusta and Savannah, the company supports a customer base across all sectors of business including private, education, government, and healthcare.

officials.name: Bernetta Lanier
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Bernetta Lanier is a native Savannahian and a fourth-generation resident of the Hudson Hill Neighborhood in West Savannah. She earned a Bachelor degree in Political Science from South Carolina State University and a Master Degree in Public Administration at Savannah State University. Bernetta has been an outspoken community advocate and organizer for the Westside of Savannah for over two decades.

officials.name: Detric Leggett
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Detric Leggett is married to Lenaida Green-Leggett and is a father of five. A 1993 graduate of Savannah High School and a 25-year veteran worker at MEMORIAL Health, he was successfully elected as the Alderman for the Second District of Savannah, GA, with over 60% of the vote.

officials.name: Dr. Estella Edwards Shabazz
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Dr. Estella Edwards Shabazz was first elected to the Savannah City Council in 2011 and is currently serving her 4th term as the 5th District Alderwoman. Dr. Shabazz is now serving for the fifth year (and second term) As Mayor Pro Temp (Assistant Mayor) from 2020 to the present time. She was unanimously elected by her Council Colleagues in both terms to serve in this as the Mayor Pro Tem (Assistant Mayor).

officials.name: Kurtis Purtee
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Kurtis Purtee was born and raised in Michigan, later attending school for Criminal Justice and entering law enforcement at 19. He moved to Savannah, Georgia in 2005, taking a police job with the Garden City Police Department, where he advanced to Captain for Georgia Southern University Police Department. He was elected District 6 Alderman in December 2019.

officials.name: Linda Wilder-Bryan
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401

officials.name: Nick Palumbo
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Nick Palumbo was elected to the Savannah City Council in 2019 and serves as the 4th District Alderman for the City of Savannah. Prior to his election, he served as the President of the Ardsley Park/Chatham Crescent Neighborhood Association where he led the neighborhood in several pioneering efforts. He previously served as a Special Agent in the United States Foreign Service and as a Federal Law Enforcement Officer with the U.S. Park Police.

officials.name: Van R. Johnson II
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Mayor Van R. Johnson II is the official head of the City of Savannah. He presides over all meetings of the Mayor and Aldermen and, as Executive Officer, signs all motions, resolutions, and ordinances passed by the Savannah City Council. As the 67th mayor of Savannah, Georgia, the Honorable Dr. Van R. Johnson II embodies purpose, passion, and a relentless commitment to people.

officials.name: Carol Bell
officials.address: P.O. Box 1027 2 East Bay Street Savannah, GA 31401
officials.bio: Carol Bell is the Alderman At Large, Post 1 for the City of Savannah.

officials.name: Alicia Miller Blakely

officials.name: Aaron V. Johnson
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Councilman Aaron V. Johnson brings nearly three decades of public service and governmental leadership to his role as the City of South Fulton’s District 2. He previously served as Chief of Staff to Atlanta City Council President Doug Shipman and District Director for Congresswoman Nikema Williams. A graduate of Morris Brown College, he is married with three children and one granddaughter.

officials.name: Jaceey Sebastian
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Councilmember Jaceey Sebastian is a dedicated Cedar Grove resident known for his unwavering passion, advocacy, and commitment to community service, including championing the incorporation of the city of South Fulton. Professionally, he specializes in market and social policy research and holds degrees in Business Administration and survey methodology. Elected as a District 4 Councilmember in November 2021, he was re-elected for a new term starting December 2, 2025, focusing on community improvements, economic development, and key legislation.

officials.name: Catherine F. Rowell
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Dr. Catherine Foster Rowell, the city's first Mayor Pro Tem, has authored over 100 pieces of legislation and holds multiple professional development certificates. With over 15 years of executive non-profit experience, she has served in leadership roles for various organizations and consulting firms. Dr. Rowell is published, serves on numerous volunteer boards, and holds bachelor's, MPA, and doctorate degrees.

officials.name: Keosha B. Bell
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Keosha Bell is a dedicated public servant, entrepreneur, and community leader, currently serving as Mayor Pro Tem and Councilwoman for the City of South Fulton’s District 5. She is the owner of Simple Pleasure Events, LLC and founder of The White Glove Experience Booking & Talent Services. With over two decades of leadership in education, workforce development, and criminal justice reform, she is committed to uplifting her community through advocacy, innovation, and service.

officials.name: LaTonya "Toni" Wright
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: LaTonya "Toni" Wright is a dedicated community leader, advocate, and proud resident of the City of South Fulton. Originally from Roanoke, Alabama, Toni has called South Fulton home for the past six years and is deeply committed to serving the residents and families who make the city a vibrant and growing community. Wright believes that strong families are the foundation of strong communities.

officials.name: Linda Becquer Pritchett
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Linda Pritchett is a first generation Cuban American and the niece of the Queen of Salsa, Celia Cruz. She raised her sons, Dakota and Logan, in District 7, where she was elected in December 2022. She began her career in the life insurance business as a life insurance agent and successfully became the owner of her own agency.

officials.name: Natasha Williams-Brown
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: A resident of South Fulton since 1978, Councilwoman Williams-Brown has deep roots in the community, graduating from Northside High School and Georgia State University. Her distinguished public service career spans more than 30 years in state government and higher education, currently working at Emory University Rollins School of Public Health. A committed volunteer and community advocate, she is a proud wife, mother, and pet parent, dedicated to serving District 6 and the greater South Fulton community.

officials.name: Carmalitha Gumbs
officials.address: City Hall 5440 Fulton Industrial Blvd SW South Fulton, GA 30336
officials.bio: Mayor Carmalitha Gumbs is a trailblazer, a leader with a deep commitment to service, equity, and community empowerment. On January 5, 2026, she was sworn in as the first woman to lead the City of South Fulton since its inception in 2017. Prior to her December 2025 overwhelming election, with nearly 60 percent of the vote, she served eight years on the City Council representing District 2.

officials.name: Robert Blakemore
officials.bio: Robert Blakemore took office as Walker County’s first District 1 Commissioner on January 1, 2021 and was re-elected to a second term that began January 1, 2023. District 1 covers northern Walker County, including Rossville, Fairview and part of Fort Oglethorpe. Blakemore is a lifelong resident of northern Walker County, working for his family owned and operated trucking company.

officials.name: David Thompson
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655

officials.name: Amarie Warren
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655
officials.bio: Amarie Warren was appointed District 1 Commissioner in 2025 and is currently serving her first term. She holds an MBA and a bachelor's degree in political science and economics, and is a local business owner. A devoted mother of two daughters, she is committed to serving Walton County with dedication and integrity.

officials.name: Pete Myers
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655
officials.bio: Pete Myers was elected District 2 Commissioner in 2024 and is currently in his first term. Myers was raised in Walton County and is a graduate of Loganville High School. A successful businessman, Myers is the co-owner of Georgia Hydrant Services, Inc. A committed family man, Myers is married to his wife, Gina, and they are the parents of three children, Marshall, McCoy and Maggie. He and his wife are both active in serving and volunteering in local schools.

officials.name: Timmy Shelnutt
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655
officials.bio: Timmy Shelnutt was elected District 3 Commissioner in 2012 and is currently in his second term. A graduate of Walton County public schools, he has been a small business owner for 30 years and is a past Chairman of the Walton County Water and Sewerage Authority. He lives in the Youth Community with his wife Gina, their three children, and a granddaughter, and they attend Corinth Christian Church.

officials.name: Lee Bradford
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655

officials.name: Jeremy Adams
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655
officials.bio: Dr. Jeremy Adams was appointed as District 5 Commissioner in 2012 and was elected in 2014 to his first full term. Jeremy owns Adams Chiropractic Clinic in Monroe. He has five active boys. The family enjoys sports and outdoor activities. They attend Gratis Church. Jeremy’s mission is to keep his district informed and to use tax dollars wisely. He is a conservative voice representing the needs of the people.

officials.name: Kirklyn Dixon
officials.address: Historic Walton County Courthouse 111 S Broad Street Monroe, GA 30655
officials.bio: Kirklyn Dixon was appointed as District 6 Commissioner in 2008. He is a graduate of the Georgia Institute of Technology and earned an MBA from Troy State University. Kirklyn owns and operates Window Genie of East Atlanta in Monroe and serves as an elder at Grace Monroe Church.
